title: Add a shared CloseButton and use it for every close button
summary: Every close (×) button in the app is now the same shared button instead of about 20 hand-made copies. Before, they ranged from 24px to 40px, some had a square hover, some a round one and some none. Now each × comes in one of three sizes, is a little muted until you hover it, and gets a round tint on hover or keyboard focus. The main thing to check is that every × still closes what it should, looks consistent, and that nothing nearby moved or broke.

links.label: PR 2161: design tokens (the step before this one)

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use the **Open the preview build** button above, in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox on a computer with a mouse or trackpad. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload.

setup.title: Make sure you're seeing the new version
setup.body: The app saves a copy of itself in your browser. If anything looks like an older version, do a hard refresh: Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, or Cmd+Shift+R on Mac. A private/incognito window also gives you a clean start.

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Some tests need you signed in. Sign in with your email: you'll get a code by email, so have your inbox handy.

setup.title: Have the live app open for comparison (optional)
setup.body: It helps to open https://alpha.seedbible.org in another tab to compare the old × buttons with the new ones.

sections.title: Panes and windows on a computer
sections.intro: What every new × should look like: about the same size everywhere, a little faded until you point at it, and a soft round shading behind it when you hover.

tests.title: Pane close buttons look the same and close their pane
steps: Open **Discover**, then close it with the × in its header.
Open your **Profile**, then close it with its ×.
Open **Settings** in the sidebar, then close it with its ×.
Before each click, hover the mouse over the × for a moment.
expected: Each × is the same size and looks slightly faded until hovered.
On hover, a round (not square) shaded circle appears behind the × and the × gets darker.
Each click closes only that pane or panel.

tests.title: Dragging a floating pane still works, and pressing × doesn't drag it
tests.before: Use a pane that floats over the reader (for example a cross reference opened from Discover, see the References test below, or any pane you can drag by its header).
steps: Drag the floating pane by its title bar to a new spot.
Press the mouse down on the pane's ×, move the mouse a little while holding it, then release over the ×.
expected: Dragging the title bar moves the pane.
Pressing on the × doesn't move the pane. Releasing over it closes the pane.

tests.title: Discover's header row is a little shorter
tests.why: Discover's × used to be 40px and the tallest thing in its header row; it's now 32px like other panes, so the row is about 8px shorter.
steps: Open **Discover** in this tab and in the live app tab, and compare their header rows.
expected: The preview's × is smaller and the header row is slightly shorter.
The title and other header buttons still line up neatly, with nothing cut off.

tests.title: References pane shows a filled round ×
steps: Open **Discover** on a chapter with cross references (for example **John 3**).
In the **Cross references** results, click a reference to open it in its own pane.
Look at the right end of that pane's header.
expected: The × sits on a soft filled circle, matching the round button beside it (the one that switches the pane between floating and docked).
Clicking the × closes the References pane.

tests.title: Modals close from their ×
steps: Open a chapter with footnotes (for example **John 1** in a translation with footnotes) and click a footnote marker. Close the footnote with its ×.
Open the **Terms of service**, **Privacy policy** and **Code of conduct** (from the links in Settings or the sign-in screen). Close each with its ×.
Open the **Share** window from a verse and close it with its ×.
expected: Each modal's × is the same size as the pane ×s, faded until hovered, with a round tint on hover. (Before, these had no hover at all.)
Each × closes its modal.

tests.title: Keyboard focus shows on the ×
steps: Open the **Terms of service** modal.
Press **Tab** until the × is focused (you may need to press it a few times).
Press **Enter**.
expected: When the × has keyboard focus it shows the round tint (and the browser's focus outline).
Enter closes the modal.

tests.title: Today closes from its ×
steps: Open **Today**.
Find the × in the top corner next to the greeting, hover it, then click it.
expected: The × is a larger button on a soft filled circle.
Clicking it closes Today.

tests.title: The floating theme preview's × sits on its corner
tests.before: You need a **Custom Branding** you can edit (found in Settings).
steps: Open your **Custom Branding** for editing and go to its theme colors, where a live preview of the reader is shown.
Scroll down past the inline preview until a small floating preview appears.
Look at its ×, then click it.
expected: The × is a small solid circle sitting on the floating preview's corner, clearly visible over the preview.
Clicking it hides the floating preview (its label is **Hide preview** when you hover it).

tests.title: The Apocrypha info box closes from its ×
steps: Open the book list (click the current book name at the top of the reader).
Scroll to the Apocrypha section and click its ⓘ info button.
Close the info box with its ×.
expected: The × matches the others and closes only the info box; the book list stays open.

tests.title: The dark theme × buttons are visible
steps: Switch to the dark theme (Settings → **Theme & text**).
Open **Discover** and the **Terms of service** modal again and hover their ×s.
expected: The × is light on dark and easy to see, and the hover circle is visible against the dark background.

setup.title: Use a phone, or a phone-sized window
setup.body: Open the preview link on a phone. If you don't have one handy, make your browser window very narrow (about the width of a phone).

tests.title: The Books screen's × and Tabs button are the same size
steps: Tap the book name to open the **Books** screen.
Compare the × at one end of the header with the Tabs button at the other end.
Tap the ×.
expected: Both buttons are the same size, and the header is a little taller than before (about 4px).
Tapping × closes the Books screen.

tests.title: The sidebar's × shows only on a phone and closes it
steps: Open the sidebar (tabs) on the phone and tap its ×.
Open **Settings** and close it with its ×.
Now widen the window to desktop size (or use a computer) and open the sidebar again.
expected: On the phone, the sidebar and Settings each close from their ×, and no tint stays stuck on the × after tapping.
On a wide screen, the sidebar shows no × of its own (as before).

tests.title: The Theme & text sheet closes from its ×
steps: Open the **Theme & text** sheet.
Tap the × in its header.
expected: The sheet closes. The × has no hover tint left behind after the tap.

setup.title: Two accounts that are friends
setup.body: You need two Seed Bible accounts that are friends with each other, signed in on two devices or two browsers (for example, a phone and a computer, or a normal window and a private window). Signing in needs an email inbox you can check for each account.

setup.title: Start a live session on the other account
setup.body: On the second account, start a live shared reading session (from the **Share** window, choose **Share current session**). Don't join it on your first account yet.

tests.title: The sharing card's × dismisses it, even on a slightly missed tap
steps: On your first account, wait for the card near the top right saying your friend **is sharing — click to join**.
Hover the × at the right of the card.
Click (or tap) just above or below the round circle around the ×, still within the card's height on the × side.
expected: The × is a small round button with a round tint on hover.
The click dismisses the card. It does **not** join the session.

tests.title: The chat panel and participants sheet close from their ×
tests.before: Start a new session from the second account, and this time join it from the first account.
steps: Open **Chat** in the session. Close the floating chat panel with its ×.
On a phone-sized screen, open the list of people in the session and close it with its ×.
expected: The chat panel's × is a small button on a soft filled circle and closes the chat panel.
The participants sheet closes from its ×.

setup.title: Get the donation box to appear
setup.body: The donation box shows only once per browser. Use a fresh private/incognito window, sign in, open **Settings** → **Extensions**, turn on **AI Transcript**, then open the **AI Transcript** panel. The donation box should appear.

tests.title: The donation box's × matches the rest and closes it
tests.why: This box draws itself outside the rest of the app, so it needed extra wiring for the shared button to work there.
steps: Look at the × at the top of the donation box and hover it.
Click the ×.
expected: The × looks like the others (same size, round tint on hover).
Clicking it closes the donation box, and the rest of the app keeps working.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: × buttons that clear or remove something still work
tests.why: These were left alone on purpose, since they clear or remove rather than close.
steps: Type something in a search box and clear it with its ×.
If you have a bookmark, remove it with its ×.
Open the verse toolbar on a phone-sized screen and use its back/close button.
expected: Each one still does what it did before and looks the same as in the live app.

notCovered: The "Hide note" × on a scripture note in a playlist also moved to the shared button. It's hard to reach without a playlist that has notes; if you have one, check that its × hides the note.
A pane or modal that can't be closed yet greys out its ×. This depends on a rarely used setting and is covered by automated tests.
Screen reader names and the new code extensions can use are covered by automated tests.
